h1: Homey Dormy Chiangrai — a warm family-run boutique stay that guests say "feels like staying with relatives in Chiang Rai"
intro: If you're tired of big chain hotels that look the same in every city and want a small place where the owner remembers your face from day one — Homey Dormy Chiangrai is the name travellers mention with a smile · it's a family-run boutique B&B with just 12 rooms, set in the Rop Wiang area on Phaholyothin Road, about 700 metres from Central Plaza Chiang Rai, roughly a 10-min walk · what reviews agree on is the clean, spacious rooms, comfortable beds, and fresh breakfast with a different menu every day · there are free bikes, parking and Wi-Fi · rooms start at about THB 700/night · the average score is high, around 9.3 on Trip.com and 4.6 out of 5 from 74 reviews on Tripadvisor

body.html: Who Homey Dormy suits — to put it as briefly as possible, Homey Dormy Chiangrai is a stay for people who want "a home-like feeling" more than luxury or a full set of amenities · it isn't a big resort with a pool and spa, and it isn't a chain hotel with hundreds of staff · it's a small family-run B&B with just 12 rooms, where the whole charm lies in personal attention and a warm atmosphere · the name "Homey Dormy" already tells you it's meant to feel like home (homey) · real reviews across several platforms echo the same thing: many guests describe it as "like staying with relatives in Chiang Rai" because the owner and team look after you closely, remember guests' names, and suggest places to eat and visit like locals · the people this place suits best are couples, solo travellers and small families who drive themselves or rent a car, and who value cleanliness, quiet and friendly service over a central nightlife location or fancy amenities · on the flip side, if you're after a hotel with a pool or gym, or you want to step out of your stay and find bars and restaurants right away, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a hotel in the old town instead · but for anyone who wants a clean, quiet base at a reasonable price for getting out to Wat Rong Khun, the Black House, tea plantations and the mountains around Chiang Rai, Homey Dormy does the job so well that many guests come back to stay again

Location and getting around — Homey Dormy is at 147 Moo 13 Phaholyothin Road, Rop Wiang subdistrict, an outer suburban area of Chiang Rai city · the clearest landmark is Central Plaza Chiang Rai, about 700 metres away, reachable in roughly a 10-min walk — which puts a big mall, restaurants, a cinema, a supermarket and coffee shops within an easy walk, an advantage many small stays in Chiang Rai don't have · there are also several local restaurants and cafés scattered around within a short walk or bike ride · the straightforward note is that this place is about 2 km from the old town centre and the Chiang Rai clock tower, so if you want to wander the night bazaar or the walking street in the evening, you'll need to drive, ride a motorbike or call a Grab for about 5–8 minutes — which is why some reviews say "the location is fairly far if you don't have a car" · the airport is an advantage, since it's only about 9–11 km from Mae Fah Luang Chiang Rai Airport (CEI), or a 15-min drive, very convenient for people who fly in and then rent a car to explore · in short, this place suits people with a car or willing to call a ride now and then, more than those who want to walk into town for everything

"It felt more like staying with relatives than at a hotel. The owners are so lovely, remembered our names, and kept recommending restaurants and the route to Wat Rong Khun · the room was spotless, the bed comfortable, and it's a ten-minute walk to Central. Great value at this price."

Room types and decor — being a small stay, Homey Dormy has just 12 rooms in total, so every room gets thorough care · the main room types you'll find in reviews and booking channels are Superior Double Room (King bed, about 30 sqm), Standard Twin Room (two single beds) and Deluxe Double Room (King bed, a larger room up to about 50 sqm) · what reviews most agree on is that the rooms are spotless and more spacious than you'd expect at this price, with many using words like "sparkling clean" and "spacious" · the decor is simple, warm and bright-toned, focused on being easy on the eye and practical rather than flashy, which fits the home-like concept · every room has air conditioning, a TV, a fridge, a kettle for tea/coffee, free drinking water, and an en-suite bathroom with a hot shower that foreign reviews single out for praise, saying the water pressure really is strong (one review says it's the best hot shower they came across on their whole Thailand trip) · there's a hairdryer and free toiletries · some rooms have a private balcony looking out over the property's garden, a favourite spot for morning coffee · if you want an especially spacious room or one with a balcony, ask when you book, since there are few rooms and they fill up fast in the cool season

Facilities and common areas — it has to be said upfront that Homey Dormy is a small B&B, so there's no swimming pool, gym or spa · some older reviews complained that a booking-site listing once said there was a pool when there actually isn't, so if a pool matters to you, rule this place out from the start to avoid disappointment · what the place does have, and does well, are spaces that create a warm atmosphere — there's a garden and terrace to relax in, a home-style common sitting area, and a small restaurant for serving breakfast · the genuine free perk is free bikes to borrow, perfect for riding to Central Plaza or pedalling around the neighbourhood in the cool morning air · there's also free private parking (very important for people driving themselves) and free Wi-Fi in the common areas and rooms · overall the facilities here are "just right" for this type of stay — not extensive, but enough for using it as a base to relax and head out, and a good fit for the price

Breakfast — this is one of the most talked-about and praised parts of Homey Dormy · breakfast is included in the room rate, made fresh every day, with a menu that changes and doesn't repeat · reviews say they had Western, American and Asian dishes, served roughly 7:00–10:00 AM · what sets it apart from a typical hotel buffet is that breakfast is cooked fresh to order, home-style, not kept warm in trays, and the owner often asks what you'd like to eat or whether you have any dietary restrictions and adjusts accordingly — a detail that makes guests feel especially looked after · a small note from reviews is that some people wished for more protein options or things like yoghurt at breakfast, but that's more a matter of personal taste than a quality issue · for other meals, there's no all-day restaurant here, but the walkable location to Central Plaza and the local spots nearby help a lot — most guests head out to eat, which is the normal way of staying at a B&B anyway

Service — if there's one thing at the heart of Homey Dormy, it's this · friendly, attentive service is what nearly every review rates as the number-one highlight · because it's family-run, the owner and team look after guests closely, and many reviews use phrases like "incredibly friendly and attentive" and "always willing to help" · guests say they got advice on routes to Wat Rong Khun, the Black House, tea plantations, car rental and local restaurants of a kind you won't get from a big hotel · it's this family atmosphere that makes many guests feel warmly welcomed and impressed enough to come back or recommend it on · of course, the trade-off of a small stay is that there's no 24-hour front desk like at a big hotel, and at certain times the owner may not be on site the whole time, so if you arrive late or have special requests, you should make your check-in time clear in advance · but overall, the service is the main reason the score here is high and reviews are consistently positive

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — gathered from Trip.com, Tripadvisor, Booking.com and Agoda, the picture is fairly consistent · on the praise side: friendly, family-style attentive service, spotless rooms more spacious than the price suggests, comfortable beds, strong hot showers, fresh breakfast with a daily-changing menu, a quiet atmosphere good for relaxing, free bikes and parking, and a ten-minute walk to Central Plaza · many sum it up as "great value" and "like staying with relatives" · on the gripe side: the most-mentioned point is that the location is fairly far from the old town centre (about 2 km), which isn't very convenient without a car, since you have to call a ride into town in the evening · next is no swimming pool (and a booking-site listing once misled people into thinking there was one), some wished breakfast had more protein/yoghurt options, the stay has stairs which makes it inconvenient for anyone with mobility issues or heavy luggage, and one older review mentioned insects, which was an isolated case · most of these gripes are about setting the right expectations (knowing it's a small B&B with no pool, on the edge of town) rather than quality problems that would stop people coming back

"The room was very clean and bigger than I expected, and the hot shower had the best pressure of the whole trip · the only downside is it's fairly far from the old town. We'd rented a car so it was no problem, but without one you might need to call a Grab fairly often."

Price comparison and value — room rates at Homey Dormy start at about THB 700–800/night in the normal-price range (around $21–28 as shown on several platforms), and can climb to around THB 1,000–1,400+ in the cool season (November–January), long weekends or festivals, with the average rate seen around THB 1,000/night · the larger Deluxe room sits in a slightly higher range depending on size and timing · compared with similar stays in Chiang Rai — small guesthouses and B&Bs in town — Homey Dormy feels like great value in the mid-price group, especially when you factor in the clean, spacious room, fresh breakfast made daily, free bikes and parking, and attentive family-style service, many of which are extras that hotels at the same price often don't include · if you plan to drive around Chiang Rai and use the stay as a quiet base, the money you spend goes a long way · but if you weigh a walkable in-town location or amenities like a pool more heavily, paying extra for a hotel in town may be better value for your style

What to know before booking — a few things will help your stay go smoothly · one, plan your transport well — this place is on the edge of town, about 2 km from the old town, so if you're not driving or renting a car, budget for a Grab/motorbike into town in the evening, or use the free bikes for nearby trips · two, don't expect a pool or resort-style amenities — this is a small B&B that sells cleanliness and service, not a full-service hotel · three, if you want an especially spacious room or one with a balcony, ask when you book, since there are only 12 rooms and they fill up fast in the cool season · four, give advance notice of your check-in time, especially if you arrive late, because it's a family stay with no 24-hour front desk · five, if you have trouble with stairs or heavy luggage, ask about a ground-floor room before booking · six, in Chiang Rai's cool season the good stays fill up fast and prices rise, so book ahead, compare prices across several platforms, and pick free cancellation if your plans aren't firm yet

Verdict — from all the real reviews, Homey Dormy Chiangrai is the stay best suited to people who want a small, clean, quiet place with warm family-style service at a reasonable price, with a car or willing to call a ride now and then · the clean, spacious rooms, fresh breakfast made daily, strong hot showers, free bikes and parking, and owners who look after you like family give it a high score and consistently positive reviews — around 9.3 on Trip.com and 4.6 out of 5 from 74 reviews on Tripadvisor (ranked #16 of 157 B&Bs in Chiang Rai) · if you're after a hotel with a pool or gym, or you want to walk straight into the old town and night bazaar, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a stay in the city centre instead · but for a road trip around Chiang Rai and its surroundings where you want a warm, clean base on a manageable budget with genuine home-style service — Homey Dormy is the kind of choice many guests stay at and say "I'll be back."

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Homey Dormy Chiangrai

faq.q: Where is Homey Dormy Chiangrai · can you walk to Central Plaza?
faq.a: It's at 147 Moo 13 Phaholyothin Road, Rop Wiang subdistrict, a suburban area of Chiang Rai · about 700 metres from Central Plaza Chiang Rai, roughly a 10-min walk · it's about 2 km from the old town centre and clock tower (5–8 min drive) and about a 15-min drive from Mae Fah Luang Airport — best for people who drive themselves or rent a car

faq.q: How much does Homey Dormy Chiangrai start at · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 700–800/night for a Superior Double Room in the normal-price range · there's a Standard Twin Room and a Deluxe Double Room (a spacious room about 50 sqm, some with a balcony) at an average rate of around THB 1,000/night · prices rise in the cool season (Nov–Jan) and during festivals, and with only 12 rooms it fills up fast, so book ahead and compare several platforms

faq.q: Who is Homey Dormy Chiangrai for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, solo travellers and small families who drive themselves and value cleanliness, quiet and warm family-style service · use it as a base to visit Wat Rong Khun, the Black House, tea plantations and the mountains around Chiang Rai · if you're after a hotel with a pool or want to walk straight into the old town, a stay in the city centre may suit you better

faq.q: Does Homey Dormy have a swimming pool and breakfast?
faq.a: No swimming pool — it's a small 12-room B&B (a booking-site listing once misled people into thinking there was a pool; there isn't one now) · as for breakfast, it's included in the room rate and made fresh every day, with a menu that doesn't repeat — Western, American and Asian, served around 7:00–10:00 AM, and adjusted on request · there are free bikes, parking and Wi-Fi

faq.q: Is getting around Chiang Rai from Homey Dormy easy without a car?
faq.a: Straight up, it's most convenient with a car or rental, since the stay is on the edge of town about 2 km from the old town · without a car, you can use the free bikes to reach Central Plaza and nearby areas, or call a Grab/motorbike into town in the evening (about 5–8 minutes) — it's worth budgeting for this transport

faq.q: Are there any downsides to know before booking?
faq.a: Points noted in reviews are that the location is about 2 km from the old town centre and isn't very convenient without a car, there's no swimming pool, the stay has stairs that are inconvenient for those with mobility issues, and some wished breakfast had more protein/yoghurt options · most of it is about setting the right expectations; the average score is still high, around 9.3 on Trip.com and 4.6/5 from 74 Tripadvisor reviews
